blocks.label: Listing Images
blocks.description: Main image rules, the seven AI-generated slots with a prompt for each, and dimensions that pass Amazon's checks.

blocks.content: The Single Most Important Image

If you fix only one thing on your listing, fix the main image. It is the image that appears in search results, comparison grids, sponsored placements, and the listing header itself. Customers decide whether to click your listing based on this single image in a fraction of a second, often before they read the title. A clean, well-lit main image lifts click-through rate by a factor of three to five over a busy or off-brand one, and click-through rate compounds into every metric downstream.

Amazon's rules for the main image are strict and they are enforced. The background must be pure white (RGB 255, 255, 255), the product must fill at least 85% of the frame, and there must be no text, badges, props, hands, models, watermarks, or branding overlays. Break any of those and Amazon may strip the image or suspend the listing without warning. The good news is that AI image generators now produce compliant white-background product shots in seconds, and we walk through that workflow below.
The Seven Image Slots

Amazon gives you seven image slots per listing. Slot one is the main image, with the strict rules above. The other six are 'secondary' images and have almost no rules: lifestyle shots, infographics, size comparisons, ingredient close-ups, packaging shots, and a second lifestyle frame. Each one is a chance to answer a customer's silent question before they ask it. Fill all seven. Listings with seven images outconvert listings with one by 20 to 30%, and the slots are free.
Generating Images With AI

Every one of the seven image slots can be generated with AI. ChatGPT (with image generation), Midjourney, Google Gemini, and free tools like Bing Image Creator all produce passable Amazon-grade product shots from a written prompt. The interactive guide above gives you a ready-made AI prompt for each of the seven slots; tap a slot, fill in the curly-brace placeholders with your bundle's specifics, and paste the prompt into the generator of your choice. The descriptive accuracy of your placeholders matters; the more specific you are about colour, material, finish, and quantity, the more closely the AI gets to your real bundle.

AI has one consistent weakness: small legible text. If a slot needs precise text rendered on the image (a benefit callout, a numbered step badge, a quantity label), the AI will sometimes produce garbled or mis-spelled text. The fix is not to abandon AI; it is to use Canva as a polish layer on top of the AI image. Generate the visual base with AI, drop it into a Canva listing template, and add the text in Canva where it will render cleanly. This combination of AI for visuals plus Canva for text is what produces all seven images in a single focused session.
Canva as the Polish Layer

Canva is the right tool for anything that needs sharp text on top of an AI-generated image. Its free tier includes Amazon listing image templates already sized to 2000 × 2000 with the safe-zone marked. Workflow: generate the product image with AI, save it locally, open a Canva listing template, drop the AI image in as the background, and layer your text and icons on top in Canva. Save each listing as its own Canva project so you can re-use the styling on future bundles.

If you have never opened Canva before, the tutorial below is a beginner-friendly walkthrough of building Amazon listing images from scratch. Watch it once before your first listing and the workflow above will make a lot more sense visually.

blocks.label: How to Make Amazon Listing Images in Canva (Beginner Tutorial)
blocks.description: YouTube tutorial, opens in a new tab. Around 15 minutes, no Canva experience needed.

blocks.content: One hard Canva rule: never use text smaller than 50 pixels on a 1600 × 1600 canvas. Anything smaller is illegible on a mobile screen, which is where the majority of Amazon traffic lives. Big text reads. Small text gets ignored. The same principle applies when you let the AI generate text directly inside the image; if the AI keeps producing tiny illegible text, add a line to the prompt asking for 'large sans-serif text at least 50 pixels tall'.

💡 The image batch rhythm: generate or shoot all seven images in one focused session, then review them as a set before uploading. Listings where each image was made in isolation tend to feel inconsistent. Listings where all seven were made in one sitting feel like a brand.

blocks.label: Completing the Form & Going Live
blocks.description: Dimensions, weight, compliance, search terms, pricing, and the final pre-submit checklist.

blocks.content: The Last Mile of the Form

With your brand sorted, your copy polished, your description converted, and your seven images uploaded, the listing form still has several pages of structured fields left to fill in. None of them is creative work; they are the operational details Amazon needs to physically receive, store, ship, and tax your product. They are easy to rush through and easy to get wrong, and the cost of getting them wrong is high: inflated FBA fees, blocked inbound shipments, account-health flags, or a listing that simply will not publish.

The interactive walkthrough below groups these remaining fields into four sections: dimensions and weight, compliance declarations, backend search terms, and pricing. Tap each section, then tap individual fields to see exactly what each one means, how to fill it correctly, and the specific pitfall to avoid. Before you open the dimensions section, take a moment with the measurement diagram below; it covers the L × W × H convention used by the form for anyone who has not measured a parcel before.
Backend Search Terms Are Where New Sellers Leak Traffic

Backend search terms deserve a second mention on their own because almost every new seller either ignores them entirely or fills them with the same words already in the title, both of which throw away free traffic. The field is invisible to the customer but fully indexed by Amazon's search algorithm, which means every word you put in there adds keyword surface area without using up a single character of your title or bullet space. Used properly, this field is the easiest extra search rank you will ever get.

The rule is simple: the words in your backend search terms field should be words a customer might type that do NOT already appear in your title. Common spelling variants (cutlery / cutlary), regional phrasings (silverware as a US-flavoured search), alternate descriptors (flatware, dinnerware), and product-adjacent terms (knife and fork) all belong here. You have a 250-byte budget, which works out to roughly 250 plain-text characters; separate the words with spaces, not commas, and never repeat a word that is already in your title.

🎯 Audit your backend terms every few weeks. Amazon silently strips entries that violate its policy (competitor brand names, subjective claims like 'best', repeated words). The field will look like it published, but no traffic comes from it. The only way to catch this is to search for your own keywords and confirm you appear; if you do not, your backend terms got stripped and you need to rewrite them.
We Do Not Use Automated Pricing

When you set your price, the form will offer to enable automated pricing rules that move your price up and down in response to competitor moves. Leave that switch off. On a new listing with no review history and no proven velocity, auto-pricing tools tend to race competitors to the bottom, which trains Amazon's algorithm to treat your price band as low and locks you out of the margin you actually need. Price manually using the formula from Module 3 Lesson 5 (single-unit Amazon price × bundle count, minus 10 to 15%), then adjust by hand based on real conversion data over the first month. Manual control is slower but gives you predictable economics while you are still validating, which is the whole point of the v1 listing.
Pre-Submit Checklist

Before you click the final submit button on your listing, run through this checklist. Each item is something that has bitten new sellers in the first 90 days post-publish and is preventable in 30 seconds at this stage.
Title is under 200 characters and front-loaded with your primary keyword
All five bullet points are filled, benefit-led, and under 200 characters each
Description is HTML-converted and pasted as HTML, not plain text
Main image is white-background, fills 85% of frame, has no text or props
All seven image slots are filled with at least 1600x1600 px images
Package dimensions and weight are measured with the polybag on
Country of origin matches what is printed on the product packaging
Hazmat is declared honestly (Yes if aerosols, batteries, or flammable liquids; No otherwise)
Search terms field uses keywords not already in the title, no commas, no competitor brands
Price uses the bundle pricing formula from Module 3 Lesson 5
Fulfilment channel is set to FBA
What Happens After You Submit

Once you submit, Amazon runs the listing through an automated validation, then a human catalogue review. Validation is instant: it confirms required fields are filled and dimensions are coherent. The human review typically takes 24 to 48 hours and confirms that your photos, copy, and category align. Most v1 listings publish without issue. If yours is rejected, the rejection email is specific about which check failed; fix that one thing and resubmit.

Once live, your listing has a status of 'Active' and is technically visible to customers. The catch is that you have no stock at Amazon yet. The listing exists, the URL works, but the buy box reads 'Currently unavailable'. That is fine; you are about to fix it. Module 5 covers exactly how to ship your first batch into FBA so the buy box goes live, and Module 7 covers how to start driving real traffic to it.

🎯 The next 48 hours: while the listing is in human review, photograph and weigh your bundle once more with the polybag fully sealed and an FNSKU label attached. That data goes straight into Module 5 Lesson 1, so you do not start that module empty-handed.
Module 5: Sending to Amazon

blocks.label: Preparing Your Bundle
blocks.description: What to have on the table before you start polybagging your first FBA inbound shipment.

blocks.content: Before You Touch a Single Polybag

Inbound shipment preparation is one of those jobs that takes 30 minutes if you have everything ready before you start, and three hours if you discover halfway through that you are missing a roll of tape. This first lesson is the laying-out-the-tools step. Read through the supplies list, confirm you have each item to hand, then move on to Lesson 2 to start polybagging. None of the supplies are expensive; a starter kit for your first 5-10 unit shipment lands at around £30 to £50 of one-off costs, most of which carries over to future shipments.

The checklist below splits everything into four groups: the stock itself, polybag supplies, outer-box supplies, and basic tools. Tap any row to see what to look for when sourcing each item. Tick items off as you confirm them, so the screen acts as a working checklist while you set up.

🛒 EliteFBA supplies: I am in the process of setting up an eBay shop with the exact polybags, FNSKU labels, Heavy Package warning labels, and brand-sticker rolls we use ourselves. Links will appear in this module once the listings are live. In the meantime, any UK packaging supplier will stock equivalents; the supplies checklist above tells you what to look for.
Set Aside a Quiet Two Hours

Your first inbound shipment will take longer than later ones because you are learning the rhythm. Block out two hours of uninterrupted time, clear a table, and work through Lessons 2 to 4 in one sitting. Trying to polybag in 15-minute chunks across a week leads to inconsistency (different sticker placement on different units, mismatched label scaling) and an inconsistent inbound shipment is a slower receiving experience at the warehouse. Do it once, properly, in one session.

blocks.label: Polybagging Your Units
blocks.description: The four labels and warnings every compliant FBA polybag carries.

blocks.content: What Goes On Every Polybag

Every single bundle you send into FBA goes into its own polybag, sealed, with a specific set of labels and printed warnings on the outside. Get the set right and your inbound passes receiving without flags. Miss a required label and either the unit is sent back at your cost or Amazon charges a non-compliance fee to relabel it for you. The good news: the requirements are short, consistent, and the same on every bundle you ever ship.

There are three required elements and one optional one. The interactive guide below covers each: the FNSKU label that identifies the SKU, the suffocation warning that Amazon mandates on every poly bag over 12.5 cm wide, the Do Not Separate label that keeps multi-unit bundles bundled, and the optional brand or shop sticker that doubles as your permanent brand marker for the GTIN exemption.
The Practical Sequence

Working through the polybagging in the same order every time makes the process roughly twice as fast once you have done it a few times. Lay out all of the bundles on a clean surface. Lay out the polybags next to them. Lay out the FNSKU labels (already printed, see Lesson 5 if you have not yet). Lay out the Do Not Separate labels and the brand stickers. Then for each unit in turn: place the bundle into the bag, apply the FNSKU label to the front face, apply the Do Not Separate label if it is a multi-unit bundle, apply the brand sticker, seal the bag with a quick fold or heat-seal. Move on to the next unit. A 25-unit shipment takes 25 to 40 minutes once you find the rhythm.

🛒 EliteFBA supplies: the exact pre-printed polybags with the suffocation warning already on them, plus the Do Not Separate and FNSKU label rolls we use, will be listed on our eBay shop. Links coming. Until then, search 'FBA polybags with suffocation warning' on any UK packaging supplier.

blocks.label: Packing the Outer Box
blocks.description: Outer box dimensions, weight limits, and the 15 kg Heavy Package warning rule.

blocks.content: From Polybagged Units to a Single Shippable Box

Once every unit is polybagged with the right labels, the whole batch goes into one outer cardboard box for shipping. The outer box is the only thing UPS or DPD ever sees; the polybagged units inside it are unwrapped by the warehouse on arrival. Amazon enforces hard limits on this outer box, both for physical handling safety and for warehouse logistics. Get them right at the packing stage and the shipment moves through receiving without flags.
Two hard limits and one important warning rule, all summarised below.
The Practical Pack

Pack the box so the polybagged units sit snugly with no rattle. Layer the units flat where possible (cutlery sets and similar flat bundles love this), or pack them in rows if they are upright (bottles, taller bundles). Use kraft paper or air pillows to fill any empty space; a box that rattles in transit damages the polybags and damages your account health when customers receive crushed units. Seal the box with at least three strips of 50mm packing tape across the opening seam, and one strip down each side for reinforcement.

Weigh the closed box on a scale before you create the shipment in Seller Central. The weight you enter into the wizard must match the actual weight; Amazon's Cubiscan re-weighs every inbound box and a mismatch beyond a few hundred grams triggers a non-compliance flag. If the scale reads between 15.0 kg and 23.0 kg, apply the Heavy Package warning label to the outside before you go anywhere near the carrier. If it reads over 23.0 kg, open the box, redistribute units across two boxes, and treat them as two separate shipments inside Seller Central.

🛒 EliteFBA supplies: branded cardboard outer boxes in the most common sizes, plus Heavy Package warning sticker rolls, will be listed on our eBay shop. Links coming. Any twin-wall corrugated cardboard box from a packaging supplier works in the meantime.

blocks.label: Creating the Shipment
blocks.description: The Send to Amazon wizard in Seller Central, step by step from inventory selection to label generation.

blocks.content: Tell Amazon What is Coming and Where

Once the outer box is packed, sealed, and weighed, the next step is to tell Amazon the shipment exists. This happens inside the Send to Amazon wizard in Seller Central, a multi-page flow that asks you which SKU, how many units, which box dimensions and weight, and which carrier you want to use. The wizard then generates the shipping labels and charges you the discounted Partnered Carrier rate. End to end, with your box already packed, this is about 15 minutes of clicking.
The seven-step walkthrough below covers exactly what to click and what to enter on each page, with the gotcha to avoid at each step.

🎯 Save the shipment plan in Seller Central even if you do not finish in one sitting. Half-completed shipment plans are stored under Inventory → Shipments → Working as drafts, so you can pause and come back without losing your dimension and weight entries.

blocks.label: Printing Your Labels
blocks.description: FNSKU labels, carrier shipping labels, shipment IDs, and the conditional Heavy Package warning.

blocks.content: The Five Labels an FBA Shipment Uses

An FBA shipment uses up to five different kinds of label, all of which you print yourself before the box leaves your address. Three you will print every time: the FNSKU labels (one per unit), the carrier shipping label (one per outer box), and the Amazon shipment ID label (also one per outer box, usually on the same PDF as the carrier label). Two are conditional: the Heavy Package warning if the box is over 15 kg, and the Do Not Separate label on every multi-unit polybag (already covered in Lesson 2).
Each label below shows what it is, where to print it, and where on the package it goes. Tap through them in order; together they describe every sticker your box will carry by the time it leaves you.
Printing the FNSKU Labels During Shipment Creation

The most common source of confusion is when to print the FNSKU labels. The answer: print them at the shipment-creation stage in Lesson 4, not before. The Send to Amazon wizard offers you a PDF of FNSKU labels sized to the number of units in the shipment, ready to print on standard 21-per-A4 adhesive label sheets (commonly Avery L7160 or any compatible 63.5 mm × 38.1 mm layout). Print, peel, apply one per polybag. If you have a dedicated thermal label printer, the wizard also offers a thermal-format option that emits one label per strip.

Print at 100% scale, never 'Fit to page'. Fit-to-page shrinks the barcode below the 0.4 mm minimum bar width that Amazon's scanners need to read it reliably, and a tiny shrink that looks fine to your eye can cause every label in the batch to fail at receiving. Print one test page first if your printer is unfamiliar, scan the test barcode with the camera on your phone, and confirm the FNSKU reads back as expected before you print the full sheet.

blocks.label: Shipping & Arrival
blocks.description: Partner carriers (UPS and DPD), the timeline from dispatch to sellable, and what to watch in Seller Central.

blocks.content: Hand the Box to the Carrier

With every label applied (FNSKU on each polybag, shipping label and shipment ID on the outer box, Heavy Package sticker if the box is over 15 kg), the box is ready for the carrier. Inside the UK, Amazon's partner carriers are UPS and DPD, both available through the Partnered Carrier flow in the Send to Amazon wizard. Using either of them gets you a materially cheaper rate than booking the same service at retail, because Amazon has negotiated the rate centrally and passes it through.

You have two options for handing the box over. Option one: drop the box at a UPS Access Point or a DPD Pickup Shop. Both carriers have a public locator on their UK websites and the network covers most high streets. This is the cheaper option and works well for one or two boxes at a time. Option two: book a doorstep collection through the carrier's website. Costs a few pounds more but is worth it once you are shipping a box every few days.
The Timeline From Dispatch to Sellable

From the moment the box leaves you to the moment your listing's buy box flips from 'Currently unavailable' to active, the typical window in the UK is 7 to 12 working days. The timeline below breaks down what happens in each stage and roughly how long each takes. Quiet weeks are faster; Q4 weeks (November, December, Prime Day in July) are noticeably slower because every UK Amazon warehouse is at peak load.
What to Watch in Seller Central

Once the box is dispatched, you do not need to chase. Seller Central updates the shipment status automatically as the carrier scans the parcel and as the warehouse processes it. The status progression you will see, in order, is: Working → Shipped → In Transit → Delivered → Receiving → Closed. The shipment is closed when every unit in the box has been checked into your inventory. At that point your sellable inventory count for the SKU increments by the number of units in the shipment, and the buy box on your listing goes live.

If a shipment sits in the Receiving status for more than five working days outside of peak season, that is the point to raise a case with Seller Support. Before then, the standard advice applies: do not chase. Receiving queues vary, and most shipments process inside 48 hours of arrival.

🎯 Track the first shipment daily for the first few cycles. Watching the status move from In Transit through Delivered to Receiving and finally to your inventory count incrementing is the single most satisfying moment in the whole course. After three or four shipments the rhythm becomes routine, but the first time it lands is something you will remember.
You Are Now Live on Amazon

When the shipment closes and the buy box flips, your listing is genuinely live: customers can find it, click it, and buy it. First sale usually lands within 24 to 72 hours of going live if your title, images, and price hold up under real demand. Module 6 starts the brand work that turns the v1 listing into something defensible long term, and Module 7 covers the marketing levers (PPC, keywords, A+ content) that drive serious traffic to it. For now, you have done the operational bit; the next 48 hours are about watching the data.

🚀 Module 7 – Scaling Your Brand: PPC, Keywords, Helium 10 & A+ Content
You’re now a registered brand. This module shows you how to make your listing visible, trustworthy, and profitable, using the exact tools real Amazon brands use today.
🎯 LESSON 1: Understanding Visibility vs Conversion
Before we jump into PPC and keywords, you need to understand two sides of Amazon success:
1️⃣ Visibility: can people find your product?
This is where keywords and PPC come in.
People must SEE your listing before they can buy it.
2️⃣ Conversion: do people buy once they see it?
This is where A+ content, images, reviews, and trust come in.
A listing can fail in two ways:
Lots of traffic but no purchases → conversion problem
Great listing but nobody sees it → visibility problem
Scaling means improving both.
I’ll show you how to fix each one step-by-step.
🧱 LESSON 2. Keywords: The Core of Amazon’s Algorithm
Think of keywords as the “language” Amazon uses to understand what you’re selling.
Amazon doesn’t magically know your product.
It only knows what you tell it through:
Your title
Your bullets
Your description
Your backend keywords
Your PPC keywords
🌍 Real Example
Imagine you sell a Car Interior Cleaning Duo.
Amazon won’t automatically connect you to searches like:
“car cleaning kit”
“dashboard cleaner”
“interior wipes for car”
“glass cleaner for car”

You must tell Amazon:
“This is what my product is relevant for.”
So the rule is simple:
If you’re not ranking for the right keywords, nobody can buy your product.
📌 How to find the right keywords (beginner version)
Use Helium 10 → Cerebro
Copy a competitor’s ASIN
Paste it into Cerebro
Sort by Search Volume
Choose keywords that clearly apply to YOUR bundle
👉 Beginners only need 10–20 strong keywords.
Don’t overthink it.
🧱 LESSON 3. Helium 10: Your Beginner-Friendly Toolkit
This is the tool that helped me build my company, and it removes guesswork.

💸 LESSON 5. PPC: The Engine That Drives Visibility
Most beginners think PPC is about “making sales.”
Not true.
PPC has ONE job:
Help Amazon understand what your listing is relevant for.
Once Amazon understands you, it will:
rank you higher
show you more often
reduce your PPC costs
📌 How PPC actually works
You bid for keywords → Amazon shows your product → you pay only if someone clicks.
For beginners, there are two PPC stages:
Stage 1: Data Collection (Week 1–2)
Use an Automatic Campaign
Amazon chooses keywords
You learn what shoppers use to find your product
Set £5–£10/day
Stage 2: Manual Campaign (Week 3+)
Use the data Amazon gives you
Add ONLY the keywords that converted
Exclude unprofitable ones
Basic Numbers to Aim For:
Click-Through Rate (CTR): 0.3 – 1%+
🌍 MODULE 8: Expanding Beyond Amazon

Once you’ve validated your product, built your brand, and created a stable Amazon listing, it’s time to grow beyond a single platform. In this module, you’ll learn how to expand safely and strategically into eBay, TikTok Shop, and your own Shopify website, without overwhelming yourself.
🎯 Lesson 1: Why Expand Beyond Amazon?
Most new sellers make the mistake of thinking:
“Amazon is enough.”
And yes, Amazon is huge, powerful, and absolutely the best place to start.
But it is also a platform you do not own.
By expanding into additional channels, you gain:
1️⃣ More sales, without more products
You don’t need to find new items. You simply place your existing product in new marketplaces.
2️⃣ Lower risk
If Amazon slows down or flags your listing for a day, your other channels keep selling.
3️⃣ Stronger brand legitimacy
Buyers trust brands they see across multiple platforms.
4️⃣ Long-term stability
The more platforms you’re on, the more your brand grows outside of Amazon’s control.
5️⃣ Higher business valuation
Multi-channel brands are worth far more if you ever sell your business in the future.

🔧 MODULE 9: Long-Term Maintenance & Keeping Your Amazon Business Healthy

You’ve launched, built a brand, scaled your listings, and expanded your channels. Now it’s time to maintain everything. This module teaches you how to keep sales consistent, avoid Amazon issues, monitor stock, and continue growing month after month.
🎯 Lesson 1: What long-term maintenance actually means
Most new sellers believe Amazon = passive.
But the reality is:
Amazon is semi-passive IF you maintain it correctly.
Your job now is to:
Keep your listing healthy
Keep your stock flowing
Keep your brand protected
Keep your PPC profitable
Keep your customers satisfied
Keep Amazon happy
Maintenance is simple, but it must be consistent.
🔁 Lesson 2: Weekly Maintenance Checklist
This is the routine that kept my store stable and growing.
Do these once a week:
1️⃣ Check Account Health
Go to:
Seller Central → Performance → Account Health
Look for:
Policy warnings
Performance notifications
Listing suppressions
Intellectual property complaints
Fix anything QUICKLY.
Amazon cares more about compliance than anything else.
2️⃣ Check PPC performance
Go to:
Advertising → Campaign Manager
Look at:
ACOS
Click-through rate
High-spend keywords with no sales
Converting search terms
Pause:
Wasting keywords
Bad performers
Irrelevant search terms
Boost:
Keywords that convert consistently
3️⃣ Check inventory levels
Go to:
Inventory → FBA Inventory
Check:
Units left
Inventory age
Low-stock alerts
Excess inventory notices
Reorder BEFORE stockouts.
Stockouts kill your ranking and PPC performance.
4️⃣ Check customer messages / reviews
Reply to any customer questions.
Acknowledge new reviews.
Identify repeat complaints.
Improve your bundle/packaging if needed.
5️⃣ Check your Shopify/eBay/TikTok orders
Make sure:
No orders are stuck
Shipping is fulfilled (if self-shipping)
MCF orders processed correctly
A multi-channel brand = multi-channel responsibility.
📅 Lesson 3: Monthly Maintenance Routine
Once a month, you should:
1️⃣ Review your profits
Use:
Seller Central Payments
Check:
ROI
Margin
FBA fees
Ad spend
Net payout
Make sure you’re not losing money anywhere without noticing.
2️⃣ Update your listings (light optimisation)
You can update:
Title
Bullets
A+ content
Backend keywords
Images
Update one thing at a time.
Track changes.
Avoid huge rewrites.
3️⃣ Check your competitors
Look at:
Their pricing
New images
New A+ content
New bundles
Their PPC behaviour (keywords they rank for)
